Meta ads reach: four ads at about 10,000 each do not make 40,000 people. (Example figures.)

Reach counts people, not views. Someone who saw all four ads is one person, but adding the four numbers counts them four times. The real figure could be 9,000 or 30,000. Only the platform, which knows who is who, can say.

Spend, impressions and clicks add up. Reach doesn't, across ads or across days.

Adspenta never adds reach up. Where a total would need it, it shows no number rather than a wrong one.

Worth checking: where does the "total reach" line in your client reports come from?

Adspenta's card showed 0 Google Ads accounts. There was an account.

On 1 October Adspenta connected to a real Google Ads account for the first time. The card said: "Found 0 ad accounts on Google."

Google was refusing every read. The code caught each refusal, skipped the account and reported what was left: nothing. A refusal became a zero, and the zero looked like a fact.

The card now shows Google's own words. An empty result and a failed read must never look the same on a screen.

Has a zero in one of your reports ever turned out to be an error? AI voice.
